title: Beeswax Grades: Yellow, White, and Filtered
description: Beeswax grades describe the wax itself as a material: its color, clarity, composition, and melting behavior. Yellow beeswax is the natural rendered wax, white beeswax is the same wax lightened by air and sun or by filtering, and filtered grades are graded by how clean and clear they are. All grades share the same core composition, mostly esters of long-chain alcohols and acids with hydrocarbons, and the same melting range near 62 to 64 degrees Celsius. This record specifies the grades and their test figures. It is a materials record; the beeswax-uses records cover methods such as candle making and polishing, while this record covers the wax grades those methods start from.
materials: Rendering pot and strainer (double boiler only)
instructions: Render cappings and old comb gently in a double boiler and strain the liquid wax through fine cloth.
Let the wax settle and cool, then scrape any sediment from the underside of the block.
Grade the block by color: deep gold for yellow grade, pale cream for light grade, and near-white for white grade.
Re-melt and re-filter any block with visible sediment, and record the grade on the block.
Store graded blocks cool, dry, and labeled, away from dust and strong smells, since wax picks up odors.
safety: Flammability and heat: beeswax is flammable and melts near 62 to 64 degrees Celsius. Melt it in a double boiler or a dedicated wax melter, never over a direct flame, keep water away from hot wax, and keep a lid nearby to smother any flare. Work in a ventilated room, keep children and pets out of the work area, and never leave hot wax unattended. Blends are labeled with their actual composition and are never presented as pure beeswax. Made without any slaughter-derived ingredient; plant oils and plant waxes are used in blends. Rendering uses hot wax and hot water: keep the work area ventilated and keep water out of the melting wax pot. Wax blocks are not food unless they are certified food-grade (E901).
yield: A 500 g batch of filtered wax fills 5 blocks; see the demo.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Beeswax Grades: Yellow, White, and Filtered'
BATCH_G = 500.0
UNIT_G = 100.0
LOSS_PCT = 5.0

def main():
    usable = BATCH_G * (1.0 - LOSS_PCT / 100.0)
    print(TITLE + ' - batch calculator')
    print('Batch: %.1f g' % BATCH_G)
    print('Usable after %.0f%% loss: %.1f g' % (LOSS_PCT, usable))
    print('Blocks' + ' filled (100.0 g each): %d' % int(usable / UNIT_G))
    print('Batches for 100 Blocks: %.1f' % (100.0 / int(usable / UNIT_G)))

main()
demo.expected_output:
Beeswax Grades: Yellow, White, and Filtered - batch calculator
Batch: 500.0 g
Usable after 5% loss: 475.0 g
Blocks filled (100.0 g each): 4
Batches for 100 Blocks: 25.0

title: Beeswax Furniture Polish Paste

The beeswax-uses record on wood polish covers the method of polishing; this record covers the paste as a product, with its grades and coverage figures.

Stir the blend as it cools so the waxes do not separate, and pour it into tins before it sets.
Let the paste cool fully, then test its hardness by pressing a fingertip into the surface.
Test coverage on a measured board and record the grams per square metre.
Label each tin with the full composition, the coverage figure, and the date.
